topics.title: Anchor Tag & Hyperlinks
topics.summary: The a element creates links to other pages, files, sections of the same page, email and phone.
topics.description: The **anchor** element `` creates a hyperlink - the feature that makes the web a *web*. Its main attribute is `href` (hypertext reference), the destination. ```html Visit Example ``` ### Kinds of destinations | `href` value | Goes to | |---|---| | `https://site.com/page` | An **absolute URL** (full address, other site) | | `about.html`, `../img/a.png` | A **relative URL** (relative to the current page) | | `#contact` | An element on the **same page** with `id="contact"` | | `page.html#faq` | A section on another page | | `mailto:me@site.com` | Opens the email app | | `tel:+1234567890` | Starts a phone call | ### Relative vs absolute - **Absolute**: complete address with protocol and domain - needed for other websites. - **Relative**: shorter and portable; keeps working if you change your domain. ### Linking inside a page Give the target an `id` and link to `#id`. With CSS `html { scroll-behavior: smooth; }` the scroll animates. ### Making things clickable An anchor can wrap text, an image, or even a button-like block. Link text should describe the destination: write "Download the price list (PDF)", not "click here".
keyPoints: href holds the destination; no href means it is just a placeholder anchor.
Absolute URL = full address; relative URL = based on the current file.
#id jumps to an element with that id on the page.
mailto: and tel: open email and phone apps.
Write meaningful link text, never just "click here".
pitfalls: Using onclick on a div/span instead of a real <a> or <button>.
Putting block-level layouts inside links without reason.
Unquoted URLs containing spaces or ampersands.

Welcome

Scroll down... (keep reading)

You landed here via a fragment link.

examples.explanation: The first link scrolls to the element whose id is "services".

interview.q: How do you link to a section of the same page?
interview.a: Give the target element an id and use href="#thatId" in the anchor.

interview.q: Absolute vs relative URL?
interview.a: Absolute includes protocol and domain (https://site.com/x). Relative is resolved from the current page (about.html or ../x).

interview.q: How do you create an email link and a phone link?
interview.a: href="mailto:name@site.com" and href="tel:+1234567890".

topics.title: Link Attributes: target, rel, download & more
topics.summary: target, rel (noopener, nofollow), download, title, hreflang and how to style link states.
topics.description:
Anchors become powerful with a few extra attributes.

### target
Where to open the link:
- `_self` - same tab (default)
- `_blank` - new tab/window
- `_parent`, `_top` - used with frames
- a **name** - opens in the iframe with that name

### rel
Describes the relationship to the target.
- `rel="noopener"` - stops the new page from controlling yours via `window.opener`. Modern browsers add it automatically for `_blank`, but write `rel="noopener noreferrer"` for old ones.
- `rel="nofollow"` - asks search engines not to pass ranking (user-generated links, ads).
- `rel="sponsored"`, `rel="ugc"` - more specific hints for paid and user content.
- `rel="external"`, `rel="next"`, `rel="prev"`, `rel="alternate"`...

### download
`<a href="report.pdf" download="my-report.pdf">` asks the browser to save the file instead of opening it. It works for same-origin files and blob/data URLs.

### Other attributes
- `title` - tooltip, extra info (not a replacement for good link text).
- `hreflang` - language of the linked page.
- `type` - MIME type hint.
- `ping` - tracking URLs (rarely used).
- `aria-label` - accessible name when the link only contains an icon.
- `tabindex`, `accesskey` - keyboard behaviour.

### Link states in CSS
`a:link`, `a:visited`, `a:hover`, `a:focus`, `a:active` - never remove the focus outline without providing a replacement.
keyPoints: target="_blank" opens a new tab; pair it with rel="noopener".
rel="nofollow" tells search engines not to endorse the link.
download triggers a save dialog instead of navigation.
Icon-only links need an accessible name (aria-label or hidden text).
Keep the :focus style visible for keyboard users.
pitfalls: Using target="_blank" on every link - it removes user control.
Forgetting rel="noopener" on _blank links to untrusted sites.
Expecting download to work with cross-origin URLs.

examples.title: download, target and rel
examples.html:
Download a text file

Open example.com in new tab

A nofollow link with a title tooltip

⚙️ (icon link with aria-label)
examples.js:
var blob = new Blob(['Hello from CodeRevise!'], { type: 'text/plain' });
document.getElementById('dl').href = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
examples.explanation: The download link points to a Blob created by JavaScript so no server file is needed.

interview.q: What does rel="noopener" do?
interview.a: It prevents the page opened with target="_blank" from accessing window.opener, avoiding tab-nabbing attacks.

interview.q: How does the download attribute work?
interview.a: It suggests that the browser save the linked resource instead of navigating to it; you may give a file name as its value.

interview.q: When would you use rel="nofollow"?
interview.a: For links you do not want to endorse to search engines, such as user comments or paid ads.

topics.title: Images: img, alt, size & image maps
topics.summary: Embed pictures with img, write useful alt text, set dimensions, make images clickable or map regions.
topics.description: The `` element embeds an image. It is a **void element** and needs two attributes: - `src` - the image URL (relative or absolute). - `alt` - alternative text, used when the image fails to load and read by screen readers. ```html ``` ### Good alt text - Describe the purpose and content: ✅ "A Rockhopper penguin standing on a beach", ❌ "image" or "penguin.jpg". - Decorative images get an **empty** alt (`alt=""`) so screen readers skip them. - Do not start with "Image of..." - the reader already announces it is an image. ### Size attributes Always add `width` and `height` (numbers, in px). The browser can then reserve the space and avoids **layout shift**. Use CSS `max-width:100%; height:auto;` to make it fluid. ### Other attributes - `loading="lazy"` - load only when near the viewport. - `decoding="async"`, `fetchpriority="high"` - performance hints. - `title` - tooltip. - Deprecated: `align`, `border`, `hspace`, `vspace` - use CSS. ### Clickable image Wrap the image in an anchor: ``. ### Image map `` with `` makes **regions** of one image clickable. Shapes: `rect`, `circle`, `poly`. ### Formats JPEG (photos), PNG (transparency), WebP/AVIF (modern, smaller), SVG (vectors and icons), GIF (simple animation).
keyPoints: img needs src and a meaningful alt.
Decorative images use alt="" (empty, not missing).
Set width and height to prevent layout shift.
Wrap img in <a> to make it a link; use map/area for hotspots.
Use loading="lazy" for below-the-fold images.
pitfalls: Missing alt attribute entirely - fails accessibility checks.
Using alt text like "image" or the file name.
Uploading a 4000px photo and showing it at 300px.
Putting important text only inside images.

examples.html:
Plain image with size and alt

Image link

Image map (click the left or right half)

examples.explanation: All pictures are inline SVG data URIs so the demo needs no files.

interview.q: Why is alt text important?
interview.a: It gives screen reader users a description, shows when the image fails to load and helps search engines understand the image.

interview.q: What alt value do decorative images get?
interview.a: An empty alt (alt="") so assistive technology skips them.

interview.q: How do you make an image a link?
interview.a: Wrap the img element inside an a element.

interview.q: Why set width and height on images?
interview.a: So the browser reserves space before the image loads, preventing layout shift (better CLS).

interview.q: What is the figure element for?
interview.a: To mark up self-contained content such as an image, diagram or code with an optional caption provided by figcaption.

interview.q: Can figure contain things other than images?

topics.title: Responsive Images: srcset, sizes & picture
topics.summary: Deliver the right image size, density and format to each device with srcset, sizes and picture.
topics.description: One image file does not suit every device: a phone needs a small file, a retina desktop needs a big sharp one. HTML solves this with **srcset/sizes** and the **** element. ### Resolution switching: srcset + sizes ```html ``` - `srcset` lists candidate files and their real widths (`w` descriptor). - `sizes` tells the browser how wide the image will be shown at each breakpoint. - The browser picks the best file for screen size, pixel density and network. For fixed-size images, use density descriptors: `srcset="logo.png 1x, logo@2x.png 2x"`. ### Art direction & formats: picture `` contains several `` elements and one `` fallback. The browser uses the **first** `` that matches. ```html ``` Use `type` to offer modern formats (AVIF, WebP) with a JPEG fallback, and `media` to show a different crop on small screens. ### Remember The inner `` is **required** - it carries `alt`, size and is the fallback. Tools such as squoosh.app help you create WebP/AVIF files.
keyPoints: srcset lists image candidates; sizes describes display width.
w descriptors = file width, x descriptors = pixel density.
picture + source lets you switch formats (type) or crops (media).
The inside picture is mandatory and holds alt.
The browser picks the first matching source.
pitfalls: Using srcset with w descriptors but no sizes - the browser assumes 100vw.
Putting the img element before the source elements.
Using wrong MIME types like image/jpg (correct is image/jpeg).

examples.title: picture with art direction (resize the preview)
examples.html: Narrow the window below 420px to see the other source.
examples.explanation: Real sites would point to different cropped files; here two data-URI pictures stand in.

examples.title: srcset and sizes syntax
examples.explanation: File names are placeholders; replace them with your own optimised images.

interview.q: What problem do srcset and sizes solve?
interview.a: They let the browser choose the most appropriate image file for the device width and pixel density, saving bandwidth.

interview.q: When use picture instead of just img with srcset?
interview.a: When you need different formats (AVIF/WebP fallback) or art direction - a different crop per screen size.

interview.q: Is the img inside picture optional?
interview.a: No. It is required; it is the fallback and carries alt, width and height.

topics.title: Audio Element
topics.summary: Embed sound with audio, offer several formats with source and provide fallback text.
topics.description:
The `<audio>` element embeds sound in a page with built-in player controls - no plugin needed.

```html
<audio controls>
  <source src="podcast.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
  <source src="podcast.ogg" type="audio/ogg">
  Your browser does not support the audio element.
</audio>
```

### Attributes
| Attribute | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `controls` | Show play/pause/volume UI |
| `autoplay` | Start automatically (blocked by most browsers unless muted) |
| `loop` | Repeat forever |
| `muted` | Start silent |
| `preload` | `none`, `metadata` or `auto` - how much to load in advance |
| `src` | Single file shortcut |

### Multiple sources
List several `<source>` children with a `type` (MIME type). The browser plays the **first** it supports. Any text inside `<audio>` is fallback for very old browsers.

### Formats
- **MP3** (`audio/mpeg`) - universal.
- **WAV** (`audio/wav`) - uncompressed, big.
- **OGG** (`audio/ogg`) - open, good compression.
- **AAC/M4A**, **WebM/Opus** - modern.

### Accessibility
Provide a **transcript** for spoken content. Avoid autoplay with sound - it surprises and annoys users, and browsers block it anyway.

### JavaScript API
`audio.play()`, `audio.pause()`, `audio.currentTime`, `audio.volume` and events such as `ended` allow custom players.
keyPoints: controls shows the browser player; without it nothing is visible.
Provide several source elements for format support.
autoplay usually requires muted.
Add a transcript for accessibility.
preload controls how much data is fetched early.
pitfalls: Forgetting controls and wondering where the player is.
Autoplaying audio with sound on page load.
Using a wrong type value so the browser skips the source.

examples.title: Audio element with a generated beep
examples.html: A 440 Hz tone created in memory by JavaScript:
examples.explanation: Normally you would write <source src="file.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">; here the source is a Blob so it works offline.

interview.q: Why provide multiple source elements?
interview.a: Different browsers support different codecs; the browser plays the first format it can handle.

interview.q: Why does autoplay often not work?
interview.a: Browsers block autoplay of sound without user interaction; the audio normally must be muted to autoplay.

interview.q: What goes between <audio> tags?
interview.a: Fallback content shown by browsers that do not support the audio element.

topics.title: Video, Poster & Subtitles (track)
topics.summary: Embed video with controls, multiple formats, poster images and WebVTT captions.
topics.description:
`<video>` embeds a media player for video files.

```html
<video controls width="500" poster="cover.jpg" preload="metadata">
  <source src="movie.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  <source src="movie.webm" type="video/webm">
  <track kind="subtitles" src="en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English" default>
  Your browser does not support the video tag.
</video>
```

### Attributes
- `controls` - show the player UI.
- `autoplay` + `muted` - autoplay only works for muted videos.
- `loop` - repeat.
- `poster` - image shown before playback starts.
- `width` / `height` - reserve the space.
- `preload` - `none` | `metadata` | `auto`.
- `playsinline` - play inside the page on iOS instead of fullscreen.

### Formats
| Format | MIME | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| MP4 (H.264) | `video/mp4` | Best compatibility |
| WebM (VP9/AV1) | `video/webm` | Open, efficient |
| Ogg | `video/ogg` | Rare today |

The browser plays the first `<source>` it supports.

### Captions with track
`<track>` adds a WebVTT text file: `kind` can be `subtitles`, `captions`, `descriptions`, `chapters` or `metadata`. Captions are essential for deaf users and also help people watching with sound off.

### Embedding vs hosting
Self-hosted files use `<video>`. For YouTube or Vimeo you embed their player through an `<iframe>` (see the iframe topic).
keyPoints: video works like audio but also has width/height and poster.
Use mp4 + webm sources for compatibility.
autoplay needs muted in most browsers; add playsinline for mobile.
track provides subtitles/captions in WebVTT.
Use preload="metadata" to save bandwidth.
pitfalls: Autoplaying large videos on mobile data.
No captions for spoken content.
Not setting dimensions - layout jumps when the video loads.

examples.title: Video element markup and capability check
examples.explanation: The movie files are placeholders, but the poster shows and canPlayType reports what your browser supports.

interview.q: How do you add subtitles to a video?
interview.a: Add a track element with kind="subtitles", src pointing to a .vtt file, srclang and label.

interview.q: What is the poster attribute?
interview.a: An image shown in the video area before the user starts playback.

interview.q: Why mute a video that autoplays?
interview.a: Browser autoplay policies only allow autoplay when the video has no sound, to avoid unexpected noise.

topics.title: iframe: Embedding Other Pages
topics.summary: An iframe embeds another HTML page (YouTube, maps, widgets) inside your page.
topics.description:
An **inline frame** `<iframe>` is a nested browsing context: a complete second page shown in a rectangle of your page. Typical uses are YouTube/Vimeo players, Google Maps, payment widgets, ads and live code demos.

```html
<iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/VIDEO_ID"
        width="560" height="315"
        title="Intro video"
        loading="lazy"
        allowfullscreen></iframe>
```

### Important attributes
| Attribute | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `src` | URL of the page to embed |
| `srcdoc` | Inline HTML instead of a URL |
| `title` | **Required for accessibility** - describes the frame |
| `width` / `height` | Size |
| `loading="lazy"` | Load only when scrolled near |
| `allow` | Permissions: fullscreen, camera, autoplay... |
| `sandbox` | Restrict what the frame can do |
| `referrerpolicy` | What referrer to send |
| `name` | Target for links: `<a target="frameName">` |

### Things to know
- Many sites (Google, Facebook, banks) **forbid** embedding with the `X-Frame-Options` / CSP `frame-ancestors` header. Use the site's official embed URL instead.
- Embedded third-party content can slow your page and has privacy and security implications - use `sandbox` for untrusted pages.
- `frameborder` is obsolete; use CSS `border:0`.

### Fallback
Content inside the iframe tag is shown only by browsers without iframe support - practically never.
keyPoints: iframe embeds an entire HTML page inside the current page.
Always add a descriptive title attribute.
srcdoc lets you embed inline HTML without a URL.
Use loading="lazy" and sandbox for performance and security.
Sites can refuse to be framed (X-Frame-Options / CSP).
pitfalls: Embedding a normal website URL and getting a blank frame.
Missing title attribute - screen readers cannot name the frame.
Embedding untrusted content without sandbox.

examples.title: iframe with srcdoc
examples.explanation: No network is needed because srcdoc holds the HTML directly.

interview.q: What is an iframe used for?
interview.a: To embed another HTML document such as a video player, map or widget inside the current page.

interview.q: Why might an iframe show a blank page?
interview.a: The target site blocks framing through X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors.

interview.q: Name iframe attributes for security and performance.
interview.a: sandbox, allow, referrerpolicy, loading="lazy" and title for accessibility.
